analysis.title: Where are the opportunities in fixed income?
key_insights: UBS CIO views fixed income as Attractive and favors selective exposure to medium- and longer-duration high-quality bonds, where current yields provide income, potential price gains and diversification.
Current bond yields provide a substantial cushion against further increases, and bonds could also benefit if inflation moderates or economic growth weakens.
Investors are advised to focus less on identifying the precise peak in yields and more on using current starting yields to strengthen portfolio income and diversification.
Global bond yields remain near multi-decade highs. The 10-year US Treasury yield has come off its 24-year high as equity-market risk aversion supported demand for high-quality bonds.
Inflation worries, fiscal concerns and rising hyperscaler debt issuance are keeping yields elevated.
UBS believes current market pricing of central bank tightening is too aggressive, which gives medium- to long-duration high-quality bonds scope for price gains.
UBS is more cautious on the longest-dated bonds because of fiscal sustainability concerns, growing AI-related debt issuance and the potential for term premiums to remain elevated.
UBS likes select exposure to emerging market credit and high yield debt, citing attractive income, diversification benefits and increasingly resilient fundamentals in EM credit.
In low-rate economies such as Switzerland, UBS sees merit in equity income approaches and select structured strategies.
Income-focused investors may prefer shorter maturities to reduce duration risk.
